raw_response:
I've been farming here in Quzhou County for 15 years. Started with about 80 mu, slowly built up to 225 mu. With this much land and only 4 people at home, I have to hire machines for ploughing and harvesting, and bring in workers during the busy season. I irrigate from my well — the electricity bill is high, but without water there is no crop. Last year my wheat gave about 510 kg per mu. This year I am switching to an improved variety — my neighbor used it and got nearly 600 kg. For fertilizer, I put about 23 kg nitrogen per mu on wheat. That is close to half a 50 kg bag of urea for each mu. The extension people say that is too much, but I cannot take the risk. Losing yield on 150 mu means losing twenty or thirty thousand yuan. Better to spend a few hundred more on fertilizer. I also use 8 kg phosphorus and 6 kg potassium per mu. Wheat gets rotary tillage after maize, then 4 irrigations. I spray pesticides 3 times. Maize goes on the same land after wheat. I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid — that is what everyone uses here. We do no-till sowing with a machine right after wheat harvest. Saves time and diesel. I apply 20 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, 5 kg potassium per mu. Three irrigations, 2 pesticide sprays. Should get 650 kg per mu. My chili is on 50 mu. That is where I make good money, but it needs more care. Five irrigations, five pesticide sprays — chili gets aphids and blight if you do not watch it. I use 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 12 kg potassium per mu. The dealer told me chili needs more potassium, and I saw it works on the field. Rotary tillage in spring. If the weather holds, I expect about 2500 kg fresh chili per mu. Stevia is 25 mu. A company buys it at a fixed price, so it is stable income. I apply 12 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, 8 kg potassium per mu. Four irrigations, 3 pesticide sprays. Rotary tillage. Should get about 180 kg dry leaves per mu. I think about my whole budget. If I spend too much on fertilizer, I have less for pesticide and labor. But fertilizer is not where I cut corners — grain price is low, so yield is everything.
